# Executive summary {#sec-exec-sum .unnumbered}

<!-- Purpose: headline-finding skeleton (Session 12). Bullets only — one per chapter, each
     sourced from that chapter's rendered figures. Humans expand these into prose. -->

*Skeleton only. Each bullet is the single headline finding from its chapter, with the key
number inline and a cross-reference to the figure that carries it. Connecting prose,
framing, and recommendations are written by hand.*

- **The county builds one thing.** Single-family detached homes are **85.1%** of Fauquier's
  housing stock (Virginia: 61.3%), and the **266 permits/year** issued over 2020–2025 were
  almost entirely single-family — 2–4 unit "missing middle" production is effectively zero
  across the full 2000–2025 record (@sec-inventory, @fig-structure, @fig-permits).

- **Fauquier is a bedroom community with a lower-wage local job base.** **76.4%** of
  employed residents (26,762 of 35,028) commute out of the county, and the average local
  job pays **$68,000** — a county median household income of **$130,189** built on wages
  earned elsewhere (@sec-demographics, @fig-commute-out, @fig-wages).

- **The entry-level for-sale market has disappeared.** The median sale price reached
  **$650,000** in 2025, and just **3 of 218** active listings were priced under $350,000 —
  while monthly payments on the median home rose **+152%** since 2016 against a **+81%**
  price increase and **+45%** income growth (@sec-market-ownership, @fig-price-bands,
  @fig-price-payment-income).

- **Rentals are mostly houses, and the subsidized stock is thin and aging.** Single-family
  homes carry **~68%** of all renter-occupied units and purpose-built apartments only
  **~20%**; the county's entire assisted inventory is **874 units across 13 properties**,
  **8 of which** have a subsidy expiring by 2036 (@sec-market-rental, @fig-rental-structure,
  @tbl-nhpd).

- **Burden is concentrated at the bottom, and the gap is structural.** **40%** of renters
  are cost-burdened versus 21% of owners; every AMI band runs a rental deficit for a net
  shortfall of **~3,315 units**, and only **8 of 218** for-sale listings are affordable
  below 100% AMI — buying the median home requires **$190,586**, about **$60,000** above
  the actual median income (@sec-gaps, @fig-rental-gap, @fig-ownership-gap,
  @fig-wages-costs).

- **Older adults are the most exposed group already in place.** **32%** of the county's
  9,173 senior households (2,922) are older adults living alone, and **41%** of elderly
  renter households are cost-burdened — against a rental market with little dedicated
  senior product (@sec-populations, @fig-senior-alone, @fig-senior-burden).

- **Production keeps pace with growth but not with need.** The county is projected to add
  **6,795 households by 2050**, requiring **~269 units/year** — essentially level with the
  266/year recent pace — but adding today's affordability backlog and replacement of aging
  stock lifts full-scope need to **12,457 units** (@sec-projections, @fig-production-need,
  @fig-scope-ladder).

- **Meeting that need is not possible under current zoning.** Remaining by-right capacity
  inside the eight service districts is plausibly **4,000–4,500 units** today (from an
  **8,381-unit** 2010 Comprehensive Plan baseline, net of ~15 years of permitting) — below
  even the ~7,000-unit headline need, forcing a choice among expanding service districts,
  increasing density, accepting unmet need, or absorbing rural spillover
  (@sec-conclusions).
